tweets.text: RT @lmrankhan: It’s likely that onchain products will split into two worlds. One builds for the real world compliant on/off ramps, KYC, regulated entities and deep integration with banks etc The other is credibly neutral, completely onchain protocols that can run indefinitely, are permissionless and will require no company to run them The interesting end state for the latter is that the protocols could become economically aligned with the underlying L1. Meaning instead of having a separate token with a company, they could continuously route fees toward buying and or burning the L1 token effectively becoming a revenue source for L1s that will compound value to the network forever. I believe this is a good thing. It keeps L1s economically protected from regulated products built on top eventually leaving, while pushing the underlying apps to keep growing, acquiring users, and creating more value for the network.
